advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle missing username/password from `git credential fill` with an explicit error rather than a raw KeyError.
evidence: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:28 `fields = dict(line.split("=", 1) for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if "=" in line)`
advisory.finding: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py._credential accesses fields["username"]/fields["password"] by direct indexing; if the git credential helper returns no credential (e.g. unauthenticated host, cancelled prompt) the returned dict lacks those keys and the script dies with a bare KeyError traceback instead of a clear 'no credentials for host' error.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use fields.get(...) and raise SystemExit with a clear message when either is absent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add table-driven tests for _label_ok (approved, value==1, value==-1, empty) and _session_hashtag (sanitization, truncation, empty->None, env precedence).
evidence: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:48-53 `_label_ok`: `return any(v.get("value") == 1 for v in info.get("all") or [])`
scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:56-62 `_session_hashtag`: `safe = "".join(ch.lower() if ch.isalnum() else "-" for ch in value).strip("-")` ... `return f"rebar-session-{safe[:48]}" if safe else None`

ABSENCE: no test references _label_ok or _session_hashtag. Named violating input: _label_ok({'labels':{'Verified':{'all':[{'value':-1}]}}},'Verified') must be False; _session_hashtag with REBAR_SESSION_ID='D4/D8 A7!' must yield 'rebar-session-d4-d8-a7'.
advisory.finding: _label_ok and _session_hashtag in scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py are untested pure/near-pure classifiers with non-trivial branching. _label_ok has two acceptance paths (approved dict vs value==1 in 'all'); _session_hashtag sanitizes and truncates session ids (non-alnum -> '-', strip('-'), [:48], empty -> None) and picks the first matching env var. Regressions in either (e.g. accepting value==-1, or emitting an over-long/invalid hashtag) would not be caught.
scenarios: A change to the label-acceptance logic that treats a rejected label as ok ships without a failing test.
A session-id containing slashes/spaces produces a malformed hashtag path segment undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_label_ok` reject labels that carry a blocking vote (or use the fetched `submittable` field) instead of accepting any single `+1`.
evidence: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:48-53 `_label_ok` returns True on `any(v.get("value") == 1 for v in info.get("all") or [])` — no check that a blocking `-1`/`-2` is absent
scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:92 requests `o=SUBMITTABLE` but `submittable` is never read (search_files for 'submittable' in scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py returned no matches)
config.py:275 `llm_review_block_value: int = -1` — the review system uses -1 as a blocking value that this helper's gate ignores
advisory.finding: `_label_ok` treats a single `value == 1` entry as label approval and never inspects the `submittable` field, so a label carrying BOTH a `+1` and a concurrent blocking `-1`/`-2` (e.g. Verified -1 from a session that re-ran CI) passes the local gate. The script requests `o=SUBMITTABLE` but discards it.
scenarios: A newer patch set's votes race with an approving +1 already on the label list; the helper's local gate approves even when Gerrit considers the label blocked
Reviewer casts a blocking -1 that coexists with an older +1 entry in the `all` list
advisory.suggested_fix: Prefer gating on `detail.get("submittable")` (already requested via o=SUBMITTABLE), or in `_label_ok` also verify `not any(v.get("value", 0) < 0 for v in info.get("all") or [])` and that the max value equals the label's approving value.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Match --revision against current_revision by prefix (or resolve the full SHA) so an abbreviated SHA is not wrongly rejected as stale.
evidence: The docs instruct `--revision <current-sha>` (AGENTS.md / docs/releasing.md) without specifying full-length SHA; `git rev-parse --short` output would never match Gerrit's full current_revision.
blocking.finding: In scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py the stale-revision guard compares the user-supplied --revision to Gerrit's current_revision with exact string equality, but current_revision is always a full 40-char SHA. Passing an abbreviated SHA (the natural output of `git rev-parse --short HEAD`) makes `current != args.revision` always true, so a submit against the actually-current revision is wrongly refused as stale (exit 2).
blocking.suggested_fix: Compare with a prefix/normalization check, e.g. `if not current or not (current == args.revision or current.startswith(args.revision)):`.

evidence: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:102-107 `missing = [label for label in ("LLM-Review", "Verified") if not _label_ok(detail, label)]` ... `return 3`

ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_gerrit_submit_if_current_8b1c.py imports only GerritClient/GerritError and tests only submit_revision and add_session_hashtag; it never imports or invokes scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.main. Named violating input: main(['<change>','--revision','deadbeef']) where the GET detail returns current_revision='cafef00d' must return 2 and must NOT issue the POST .../submit.
blocking.finding: The submit-if-current safety decision in scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:main() is entirely untested: no test drives the stale-revision refusal (exit 2), the missing-label/unresolved-comment refusal (exit 3), or the success path that only submits after both checks pass. This is the core contract advertised in AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md ('the helper refuses rather than submitting stale state'), yet a regression that makes main() submit despite current_revision != args.revision would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor of the guard in main() (e.g. inverting the comparison or moving the submit call before the check) ships green because no test exercises main().
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that monkeypatches gerrit_safe_submit._request (and _credential) to return a detail dict with a non-matching current_revision, and asserts main returns 2 and the submit POST was never issued; add companion cases for missing 'Verified' label (exit 3) and the all-green success path (exit 0, submit POST issued to the revision-scoped path).

dropped.finding: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py._label_ok hardcodes `v.get("value") == 1` as the approval threshold rather than the configurable label max used elsewhere (config.llm_review_max_value). For any label whose approving value is not exactly +1 (e.g. a +2 Code-Review-style label), a legitimately approving vote is treated as not-OK, causing a false 'missing live labels' refusal (exit 3).
